title: Informational passages as long as stories
statement: Whether informational passages should run as long as narrative ones, or may stay shorter for their knowledge density, is unsettled.
example: One Grade 3 course's informational passages ran about 310–330 words against about 460–500 for its narratives.
detail: A Grade 3 reading standard lists the informational text-length floor among the bounded questions still awaiting a ruling: its informational passages run about 310–330 words and its narratives about 460–500, and it asks whether to raise the informational floor or accept it for knowledge density. Its text-quality criteria record the same open decision and keep the mechanical length check advisory for informational texts until it is ruled. Nothing measured which length serves readers.

evidence.quote: G3 informational currently runs ~310–330w; narrative ~460–500w. Raise the informational floor, or accept it for knowledge density?
The informational-text length floor (currently ~310–330 words) is unsettled; the D8.12 mechanical length check treats the informational floor as advisory until this is ruled.
